Hey Claire / Ben —

Great questions — below are concise answers and some runnable examples. I'll bring these to the tech sync and can demo a local flow.

Auth / KMS:
- Pattern: use a Redwood service account key (JSON blob) stored in AWS Secrets Manager / KMS. We provide example CloudFormation/IaC snippet that creates an IAM principal and a short-lived key rotation helper.
- For dev: set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. For CI: inject from Secrets Manager into your pipeline. See link: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk-quickstart#auth

Routing (hosted -> dedicated):
- SDK supports a 'target' param: target: hosted | dedicated:<pool-id> | private. Example (Python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), target='dedicated:acme-peak')
- We also support routing policies on the control plane so you can route by latency threshold or cost center. We'll share a sample routing policy used by a similar fintech customer.

Structured output & tool calling:
- Use our 'tools' SDK: define a tool schema (name, args, output_schema). The model will return a structured JSON payload when you call with tools enabled. Example in sample app attached (see examples/payment_tool.py).

Embeddings / rerankers:
- For small labeled sets (50-500): start with an embedding index + a lightweight logistic scorer trained on embedding distances. This is fast and cost-effective. If you need stronger relevance quickly, a small cross-encoder (distilBERT-size) on Dedicated for reranking is recommended after you have ~1k pairs.

Local testing (recommended flow):
1) Clone sample app: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme-sdk-sample (attached reference).
2) Run a local mock server that proxies to hosted sandbox endpoints; set REDWOOD_API_URL to http://localhost:8080 for the SDK.
3) Use Docker-compose for the sample which runs the mock router, a simple vector DB (FAISS container), and the sample web UI. Command: docker-compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build

I've attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (condensed), acme-integration-matrix.xlsx (filled partially), and examples/payment_tool.py + sample notebooks in the Drive link.

If this looks good, I'll provision a temporary dedicated pool for your load test next week (low-cost, short-lived) once we confirm network constraints.
